A root canal treatment helps save a tooth affected by deep decay or infection. However, after treatment, the tooth can become weaker and more prone to cracking or damage during everyday chewing.

This is why a dental crown is often recommended after root canal treatment. A crown acts like a protective cap that covers the treated tooth, helping restore its strength, function, and appearance.

• Provides added protection to the treated tooth
• Reduces the risk of cracks and fractures
• Restores normal chewing function
• Improves the appearance of the tooth
• Designed to blend naturally with your smile

When placed at the right time, a dental crown can help extend the life of a root canal-treated tooth and support long-term oral health.

Missing teeth can affect your smile, chewing ability, and overall oral health. When exploring teeth replacement options, dental implants are often considered one of the most durable and natural-looking solutions.

Dental implant treatment replaces the missing tooth root with a titanium implant that integrates with the jawbone, creating a strong foundation for the replacement tooth. This stability helps maintain bone health and allows the tooth to function much like a natural one.

• Strong and stable support for everyday chewing
• Helps preserve jawbone health
• Does not depend on neighboring teeth for support
• Natural-looking appearance and feel
• Long-lasting solution with proper care

For many patients, dental implant treatment offers a reliable way to restore both function and confidence after tooth loss.

If cold drinks or ice cream trigger sharp pain in one or more teeth, it usually indicates enamel wear, exposed dentin, or early decay.

When sensitivity becomes frequent or localised to a specific tooth, it should not be ignored.

Treatment may include desensitising agents, fillings, or restorative procedures, depending on the cause.

Along with treatment, following proper precautions helps prevent worsening of sensitivity:

•	Avoid very cold or very hot foods and drinks 
•	Reduce intake of acidic items like citrus fruits, soda, and packaged juices 
•	Use a soft-bristled toothbrush and avoid aggressive brushing 
•	Do not brush immediately after consuming acidic foods (wait at least 30 minutes) 
•	Use desensitising toothpaste if sensitivity is frequent 
•	Maintain a gentle, circular brushing technique twice daily 

Early care prevents progression into deeper decay or nerve involvement.

Saving your natural tooth preserves your bite, prevents neighboring teeth from shifting, and avoids the need for more complex replacements. If you're experiencing sensitivity, swelling, or persistent toothache, don't delay treatment.
